historyContradiction.detail: Debridement billed for a left-foot ulcer that cannot exist on a patient with a prior left below-knee amputation (Z89.512, 2023). The service was not — and could not be — rendered.

finding.summary: The note alone describes a credible left-foot ulcer debridement, and the coding expert agreed with the bill on the note-only pass. Extended chart verification revealed a prior left below-knee amputation (Z89.512, 2023) — the left foot does not exist. The billed left-foot ulcer (L97.523) and debridement (97597) are anatomically impossible: a phantom service caught only by pulling the patient history.

details.evidence: History and assessment document Type 2 diabetes with diabetic neuropathy; continued metformin and gabapentin.
History (Z89.512) records a prior left below-knee amputation in 2023. The left foot does not exist, so a left-foot ulcer cannot be present or debrided.
Debridement billed for a left-foot ulcer that cannot exist on a patient with a prior left below-knee amputation. The service could not have been rendered.
A service billed that is anatomically impossible given the patient's history — the history-dependent analogue of services not rendered, caught only by extended chart verification.

legal_brief: The documented encounter describes a left-foot diabetic ulcer with sharp debridement. The coding expert agreed with the billed codes (L97.523, 97597) on the note-only pass. Extended chart verification revealed a prior left below-knee amputation (Z89.512) performed in 2023 — the left foot does not exist. The billed left-foot ulcer and debridement are anatomically impossible and could not have been rendered. Fraud type: phantom (services not rendered). Verdict: fraud.
